title: About — BetterMapandan.org
description: About the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan, and the Better Mapandan civic transparency project.
body: About About Better Mapandan An independent civic transparency portal for the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan. About Mapandan The municipality History Mapandan was created as an independent pueblo on December 28, 1887, through Director General No. 39. After a period of financial insolvency (1905–1908) when it was re-absorbed into Mangaldan, the town was re-established as an independent municipality in 1909 under Executive Order No. 10 by Governor General James F. Smith. The town was named for the abundance of fragrant pandan plants in the area. Geography Mapandan is a third-class municipality in the province of Pangasinan, Philippines. It covers a land area of 30.00 km² and is composed of 15 barangays. The municipality is located in the western part of Pangasinan, bordered by the Lingayen Gulf to the north and the Agno River floodplain to the south. Population 38,228 PSA Census 2020 Land Area 30.00 km² MPDC Land Use Plan 2024 Barangays 15 DILG / Comelec About the Project What is Better Mapandan? Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal built and maintained by volunteers. It is part of the BetterGov.ph initiative to create open, accessible civic information websites for Philippine municipalities. Our Mission To make government information accessible, understandable, and actionable for every Mapandan resident. We believe that open data strengthens democracy and empowers communities to participate meaningfully in local governance. How It Works We compile publicly available government data — from COA audit reports, PSA census data, municipal disclosures, and provincial issuances — into a single, easy-to-navigate website. Every piece of information is sourced and attributed. Open Source The source code is publicly available. Developers can contribute, audit, and improve the platform. View on GitHub → Independent Better Mapandan is not an official government website. It is a community-run project that operates independently of the Local Government Unit. Volunteer-Run Built and maintained entirely by volunteers. No government funding is used. Cost to the people of Mapandan: ₱0. Contribute Get involved Better Mapandan thrives on community participation. Here's how you can help: Report Incorrect Information Spotted an error? Help us keep the data accurate by reporting mistakes. Report an error → Contribute Code Developers can contribute features, fix bugs, or improve accessibility on GitHub. Fork on GitHub → Verify Data Help verify government information by cross-referencing with official sources. Submit verification → Share with Residents Spread the word about Better Mapandan so more residents can access government information. Disclaimer Important notice Better Mapandan is an independent community project and is not an official website of the Municipality of Mapandan or any government agency. Information presented on this site is compiled from publicly available government sources and community research. While we strive for accuracy, we cannot guarantee the completeness or timeliness of all data. For official government information, please visit mapandan.gov.ph or contact the municipal government directly.

title: BetterMapandan.org — Mapandan, Pangasinan Transparency Portal
description: An independent, citizen-run transparency portal for the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan — officials, budget, ordinances, services, and emergency contacts, built under the BetterGov.ph BetterLGU initiative.
body: Independent · Citizen-Maintained · Pangasinan Mapandan, in the open. Officials, budgets, ordinances, and frontline services for the Municipality of Mapandan — gathered from public records and kept in one place, so every resident can find what their local government is doing. Browse Services See the Budget Find a Service Search every service Mapandan offers — by what you're trying to do, not which office handles it. Popular: business permit local hospital barangay clearance tax declaration 38,228 Official Source: PSA Census 2020 Residents 15 Official Source: DILG / Comelec Barangays 9,326 Official Source: PSA Census 2020 Households 1,274/km² Official Computed: 38,228 ÷ 30.00 km² Pop. density 30.00 km² Official Source: MPDC Land Use Plan 2024 Land area Third-Class Municipality · Region I A rice-growing town in Pangasinan's third district Mapandan sits in the Third Congressional District of Pangasinan, bounded by San Jacinto to the north, Mangaldan to the northwest, Manaoag to the east, and Santa Barbara to the south. Covering 30.00 square kilometres, around three-quarters of its land supports agriculture — mainly rice, alongside corn, livestock, and seasonal vegetables. The municipal administration operates under the tagline “Kaakibat niyo ang Aktibo at Responsableng Liderato” (Partnering with you in Active and Responsible Leadership). 01 Founded Dec. 28, 1887 Separated from Mangaldan as an independent pueblo under Governor General Emilio Bravo, led by ten local leaders including Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, and Andres Bongato. 02 Re-established 1909 A severe epidemic forced temporary re-annexation to Mangaldan. Full autonomy was restored via Executive Order No. 10 by Governor General James F. Smith. 03 Agricultural heart Approximately 75% of the municipality's 30 km² is dedicated to lowland crop production, livestock, and poultry farming. A Brief History The Story of Mapandan From a new pueblo to a growing community Foundation 1887 Survival 1903 Rebuilding 1909 Community 1940s Development 1960s Today 2002+ Before 1887 Southern barrios of Mangaldan Before Mapandan existed, the area belonged to Mangaldan as southern communities including Payapay, Baloling, Apaya, and Amanoaoac. Read the founding story Ten local leaders — Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, Andres Bongato, Ambrosio Calimlim, Valeriano Tamondong, Tomas Aquino, Fulgencio Nato, Filomeno Sarmiento, Jose Lalas, and Florencio Datuin — led the petition for a separate town. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Municipal Profile — Historical Background Dec. 28, 1887 Mapandan becomes a pueblo Established as an independent pueblo through Director General No. 39, signed by Governor General Emilio Bravo. Read more The new pueblo was initially composed of the southern barrios of Mangaldan. Its administrative seat was first set up in Barrio Torres, then relocated to present-day Poblacion on land donated by the Aquino family. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Municipal Profile — Historical Background 1887–1890s The first town center The first seat was in Barrio Torres, near a church where Fr. Jose Torres served. The town was named for the abundance of fragrant pandan plants. Read more The Torres location proved inconvenient — too close to the southern boundary. The center was eventually transferred to an area that had been a sitio of Apaya. Leon Hilario Aquino encouraged settlement by subdividing land into uniform lots. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Barangay Torres History; Barangay Poblacion History 1903 The epidemic A severe epidemic devastated the municipality, causing population loss, migration, and fiscal insolvency. The 1903 census recorded 4,198 residents. Read more The epidemic directly affected Mapandan’s ability to function as a municipality, leading to its temporary return to Mangaldan. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Municipal Profile; PSA Census 1903 1905–1908 Return to Mangaldan Due to financial insolvency, Mapandan temporarily surrendered its municipal status and was re-absorbed as part of Mangaldan. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Municipal Profile — Historical Background 1909 Mapandan rises again Re-established as an independent municipality under Executive Order No. 10, issued by Governor General James F. Smith. Read more After years of demographic and financial difficulties, Mapandan was reorganized and re-established as an independent municipality, beginning a new chapter of growth. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Municipal Profile — Historical Background 1940s War and reconstruction The Second World War interrupted development across Pangasinan. Postwar years brought land ownership changes and community rebuilding. Read more In the postwar years, tenants gained opportunities to own land they had been farming. Communities like Sta. Maria developed from hacienda land into independent barrios. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Barangay Sta. Maria History 1965 Sta. Maria becomes a barrio Formerly a sitio of Luyan on hacienda land, Sta. Maria was established as a separate barrio, marking the growth of Mapandan’s community structure. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Barangay Sta. Maria History 1967 Golden becomes a barangay Formerly Amanoaoac North, Golden was established as a separate barangay. Named after the Golden Distillery that operated after liberation. Read more Golden underwent substantial development including road improvement, waterworks, school construction, and cooperative organization. In 1972, it was recognized as a SEATO/PACD Model Village, with the award presented at Malacañang. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Barangay Golden History 1972–1973 Coral is established Created through Municipal Council Resolution No. 87 (1972), Provincial Board Resolution No. 155, and Proclamation No. 11 (1973). Named after the stone coral enclosure built during the Spanish era. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Barangay Coral History 2002 Third-class municipality Mapandan was elevated to a third-class municipality, reflecting income and revenue growth under then-Mayor Jose Ferdinand Z. Calimlim Jr. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Physical Characteristics — Historical Development 2010s The Pandan Festival grows The Pandan Festival developed into an important annual celebration of Mapandan’s identity, culture, and community, held alongside the town fiesta. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Official Website 2022–2024 Expanding healthcare access National health infrastructure funding supported the Mapandan Super Health Center. Its first phase was inaugurated on March 15, 2024, serving residents of all 15 barangays. Read more The 2022 General Appropriations Act included &₱circ;6.5 million for the facility. Phase 1 provides laboratory and dental services for Mapandan and nearby municipalities. Source: Philippine News Agency, March 15, 2024; DBM General Appropriations Act 2022 2024 Mapandan today More than 130 years after its establishment, Mapandan is a 15-barangay municipality with a population of 38,228, continuing to invest in public services and community development. Source: Philippine Statistics Authority, 2024 POPCEN Mapandan Town Plaza ← 1 / 5 → Source: Mayor Karl Vega, “History of Mapandan” — YouTube Population through time Source: Philippine Statistics Authority, Census of Population (1903–2024) Stories Behind Our Barangays 15 communities, 15 histories Each of Mapandan’s barangays has its own story of origin, growth, and community life. Sources & Historical Notes Much of Mapandan’s historical material comes from the Municipality of Mapandan’s official website, including the Municipal Profile, Physical Characteristics, and individual barangay history pages. Population data is from the Philippine Statistics Authority. Development milestones reference the Philippine News Agency and Department of Budget and Management records. Some barangay histories attribute parts of their narratives to “old folks” / local oral histories. These are labeled as local historical accounts rather than independently documented facts. Municipality of Mapandan — Municipal Profile Municipality of Mapandan — Physical Characteristics Philippine Statistics Authority — Mapandan PSGC Philippine News Agency — Super Health Center Inauguration Historical photos: Mayor Karl Vega, “History of Mapandan” — YouTube Cultural Heritage Local traditions and community life Pandan Festival Held annually during the second week of April, celebrating the town's agricultural harvest and its namesake plant, Pandanus amaryllifolius . Events include street-dancing pageants, trade fairs, and exhibitions of traditional pandan leaf weaving. Town Plaza Located in Poblacion, the Mapandan Town Plaza is widely regarded as one of Pangasinan's best-maintained civic parks, featuring an open-air auditorium, tennis courts, recreational children's playgrounds, and landscaped green space. Agri-Tourism in Luyan Barangay Luyan is highlighted in regional DOT farm-to-table culinary circuits, offering agri-tourism programs that showcase sustainable crop cultivation, local gastronomy, and rural life. 15 Barangays Where Mapandan's residents live Population figures from the 2024 and 2020 census, alongside each barangay's primary land use. title: Legislative Documents — BetterMapandan.org
description: Ordinances and resolutions passed by the Sangguniang Bayan ng Mapandan, plus the step-by-step process for enacting local legislation.
body: Sangguniang Bayan Legislative Documents Ordinances and resolutions passed by the Sangguniang Bayan ng Mapandan, and how a proposal becomes local law. Ordinances Recent municipal ordinances This list covers ordinances confirmed through provincial issuances and official municipal disclosures. More will be added as records are gathered. No. Title Key Date Status Source 5, S-2025 An ordinance creating the position of Municipal Government Department Head I (MDRRM Officer) under the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office Declared valid Dec 15, 2025 Enacted Provincial validation → 4, S-2021 An ordinance creating permanent positions for Tax Mapping Aide in the Office of the Municipal Assessor and Administrative Aide I in the Office of the Municipal Agriculture Approved Oct 4, 2021 Enacted Provincial review → — Real Property Tax penalty relief — implementation of Provincial Ordinance No. 253-2020 through the Municipal Treasury Office, condoning accrued interest and penalties on unpaid real property taxes Provincial ordinance, 2020 In effect Provincial Ord. 253-2020 → Key Distinction Ordinance vs. Resolution Under the Local Government Code of 1991, the Sangguniang Bayan enacts two types of legislative measures: Ordinance A legislative measure that enacts a permanent rule or policy . Ordinances carry the force of law, create offices, levy taxes, or regulate conduct. They require three readings, publication, and the Mayor's approval (or passage by 2/3 override of a veto). Resolution A legislative measure that expresses the sentiment, intent, or opinion of the Sangguniang Bayan on a specific matter. Resolutions are used for internal housekeeping, requesting national action, or authorizing one-time transactions. They require only one reading and are not subject to publication. Provincial Provincial Resolution No. 272-2022 A key provincial resolution supporting LGU infrastructure cooperation. No. Title Date Status 272, S-2022 A resolution endorsing the construction and rehabilitation of farm-to-market roads and flood control structures under the Provincial Government's infrastructure program, including projects benefiting the Municipality of Mapandan 2022 Adopted Source: Provincial Government of Pangasinan issuances Process Flow How an ordinance becomes law The standard path a proposal follows through the Sangguniang Bayan, under the Local Government Code of 1991. 1 Filing A proposed ordinance is filed with the Sangguniang Bayan for consideration. 2 First Reading Initial reading and referral to the relevant committee for review. 3 Committee Hearing The committee holds hearings and deliberates on the proposal. 4 Committee Report Findings and recommendations are submitted back to the full council. 5 Second Reading Detailed floor discussion and debate on the proposed ordinance. 6 Third & Final Reading Final vote by the Sangguniang Bayan. 7 Mayor's Approval The Municipal Mayor reviews and approves the enacted ordinance. 8 Posting & Effect The approved ordinance is posted publicly and takes effect within the municipality. Precedent A landmark case tied to Mapandan Navarro v. Court of Appeals (G.R. No. 141307, March 28, 2001) arose from a succession within Mapandan's local government. When Vice Mayor Baltazar Aquino assumed the mayoralty, the highest-ranking Sangguniang Bayan member elevated to Vice Mayor, opening a legislative seat. The Supreme Court ruled that the replacement had to come from the same political party as the vacating member, a precedent that continues to guide multi-tier local successions nationwide under Sections 44 and 45 of the Local Government Code.

title: Agricultural Subsidies — BetterMapandan.org
description: Apply for government-subsidized agricultural programs in Mapandan. Learn about eligibility, requirements, and available assistance from the MAO.
body: Health, Social Welfare & Agriculture Agricultural Subsidies Apply for government-subsidized agricultural programs in Mapandan. Learn about eligibility, requirements, and available assistance from the MAO. Home › Services › Agricultural Subsidies Description The Municipal Agriculture Office (MAO) provides various government-subsidized agricultural programs to support local farmers and fisherfolk in Mapandan. These programs include subsidies for seeds, fertilizers, farm equipment, and technical assistance to improve agricultural productivity and livelihood. Availability of subsidies depends on national and provincial funding allocations. Requirements Farmer registration with the Municipal Agriculture Office Barangay certification of residency and farming activity Farm location and land area information Procedure Register with the Municipal Agriculture Office (MAO) as a farmer or fisherfolk. Secure a barangay certification confirming your farming activity and residency. Submit your registration and requirements to the MAO. Wait for availability announcement of agricultural subsidies or programs. Receive agricultural assistance or subsidies upon program approval. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Agriculture Office (MAO) Classification: Simple Processing Time: Varies (depends on availability) Fee: Free (government-subsidized) Where to Apply: Municipal Agriculture Office, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1873 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Health Consultation • AICS Assistance

title: AICS Assistance — BetterMapandan.org
description: Apply for Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS) in Mapandan. Learn about requirements, eligibility, and how to get help from the MSWDO.
body: Health, Social Welfare & Agriculture AICS Assistance Apply for Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS) in Mapandan. Learn about requirements, eligibility, and how to get help from the MSWDO. Home › Services › AICS Assistance Description Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS) is a government program that provides financial assistance to individuals and families facing emergencies such as medical crises, bereavement, or other unforeseen circumstances. In Mapandan, AICS assistance is administered by the Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSWDO) in coordination with the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD). Requirements Barangay certification stating the resident’s crisis situation Medical certificate (for medical-related assistance) Death certificate (for burial assistance) Valid government-issued ID Case study or social worker assessment Procedure Secure a barangay certification from your barangay captain or kagawad. Gather all required documents (medical certificate, death certificate, etc.). Visit the MSWDO office and submit your application with supporting documents. Wait for the social worker’s assessment and case study. Receive financial assistance upon approval of your application. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSWDO) Classification: Simple Processing Time: 1–3 working days Fee: Free Where to Apply: MSWDO Office, Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1751 / 0930-641-3934 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Health Consultation • Senior Citizen / PWD ID

title: Birth Certificate — BetterMapandan.org
description: Requirements, fees, and step-by-step procedure for requesting a birth certificate from the Municipal Civil Registrar of Mapandan, Pangasinan.
body: Civil Registry & Vital Records Birth Certificate Request a certified copy of your birth certificate from the Municipal Civil Registrar of Mapandan. Home › Services › Birth Certificate Description A birth certificate is a vital record that serves as proof of identity, age, and Filipino citizenship. The Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) of Mapandan issues certified copies of locally registered birth certificates. This document is required for school enrollment, passport application, employment, and other legal purposes. Requirements Valid government-issued ID of the requesting party PSA copy of the birth certificate (if available, for verification) Barangay certification of residency (for the person named on the certificate) Affidavit of two disinterested persons (required for delayed registration only) Procedure Visit the Municipal Civil Registrar’s Office and present valid identification. Fill out the request form and provide the necessary supporting documents. Pay the certification fee at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Receive the certified birth certificate upon release. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) Classification: Simple Processing Time: 3–5 working days Fee: As scheduled by the MCR (varies by copy type) Where to Apply: Municipal Civil Registrar’s Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Marriage License • Death Certificate • Name Correction (RA 9048)

title: Building Permit — BetterMapandan.org
description: Requirements, fees, and step-by-step procedure for applying for a building permit in the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan.
body: Building, Engineering & Zoning Building Permit Secure a building permit before commencing any construction or renovation in the Municipality of Mapandan. Home › Services › Building Permit Description A building permit is a legal requirement under the National Building Code of the Philippines (PD 1096) for any construction, renovation, alteration, or demolition of a building or structure. The Municipal Engineering Office (MEO) of Mapandan reviews and issues building permits after ensuring compliance with safety standards, zoning, and structural requirements. Requirements Approved zoning clearance from the MPDC Architectural plans (signed and sealed by a licensed architect) Structural plans (signed and sealed by a licensed civil/structural engineer) Bill of materials and cost estimate Certificate of land title or ownership documents Tax clearance / latest real property tax payment Procedure Obtain a zoning clearance from the MPDC / Zoning Office. Prepare architectural and structural plans signed by licensed professionals. Submit all documents to the Municipal Engineering Office (MEO) for review. Pay the building permit fees at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Receive the approved building permit after technical evaluation. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Engineering Office (MEO) Classification: Highly Technical Processing Time: 10–15 working days Fee: Based on project cost (schedule per National Building Code) Where to Apply: Municipal Engineering Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Zoning Clearance • Occupancy Permit

description: Requirements, fees, and step-by-step procedure for applying for a new business permit in the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan.
body: Business Permitting & Licensing New Business Permit Secure your new business permit to operate commercially in the Municipality of Mapandan. Home › Services › New Business Permit Description A business permit is required for all individuals or entities intending to operate a commercial business within the Municipality of Mapandan. This permit is issued after compliance with documentary and safety requirements and upon payment of applicable fees. Requirements DTI or SEC registration certificate Barangay clearance from the barangay where the business is located Fire safety inspection certificate Occupancy permit (if renting a commercial space) Sketch of business location Valid government-issued ID of the business owner or authorized representative Procedure Secure a barangay clearance from the barangay where the business will be located. Gather all required documents and submit them to the Municipal Treasurer’s Office (MTO). Pay the corresponding business permit fees based on your business category. Receive your official business permit upon successful processing. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Treasurer’s Office (MTO) Classification: Simple Processing Time: 3–5 working days Fee: Based on business category (schedule available at MTO) Where to Apply: 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Business Permit Renewal • Special Event Permit

title: Business Permit Renewal — BetterMapandan.org
description: Requirements, fees, and step-by-step procedure for renewing your business permit in the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan.
body: Business Permitting & Licensing Business Permit Renewal Renew your existing business permit to continue operating in the Municipality of Mapandan. Home › Services › Business Permit Renewal Description Businesses operating within Mapandan are required to renew their business permits annually. Renewal ensures that your business remains compliant with local regulations and avoids penalties for late filing. Requirements Previous year’s business permit Updated DTI or SEC registration certificate Latest Barangay clearance Fire safety inspection certificate Valid government-issued ID of the business owner Procedure Secure an updated barangay clearance from your barangay. Submit all required documents to the Municipal Treasurer’s Office (MTO). Pay the renewal fee based on your business category. Receive your renewed business permit. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Treasurer’s Office (MTO) Classification: Simple Processing Time: 1–3 working days Fee: Based on business category (schedule available at MTO) Where to Apply: 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services New Business Permit • Special Event Permit

title: Cedula / Community Tax Certificate — BetterMapandan.org
description: Obtain your community tax certificate (cedula) in Mapandan. Learn about fees, requirements, and where to apply.
body: Real Property & Revenue Administration Cedula / Community Tax Certificate Obtain your community tax certificate (cedula) in Mapandan. Learn about fees, requirements, and where to apply. Home › Services › Cedula / Community Tax Certificate Description The Community Tax Certificate, commonly known as a cedula, is a requirement for residents of Mapandan engaged in certain transactions with government agencies. It serves as proof of community tax payment and is required for various legal, business, and personal transactions. The cedula is issued under the provisions of the Local Government Code (Republic Act No. 7160). Requirements Valid government-issued ID Payment of community tax Procedure Present your valid ID at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Pay the basic community tax of ₱500. If applicable, pay an additional ₱1 per ₱1,000 of gross income earned during the preceding year. Receive your community tax certificate (cedula). Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Treasury Office (MTO) Classification: Simple Processing Time: Same day Fee: ₱500 (basic community tax) + ₱1 per ₱1,000 of income (if applicable) Where to Apply: 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Real Property Tax Payment • Tax Declaration Copy

title: Death Certificate — BetterMapandan.org
description: Requirements, fees, and step-by-step procedure for requesting a death certificate from the Municipal Civil Registrar of Mapandan, Pangasinan.
body: Civil Registry & Vital Records Death Certificate Request a certified copy of a death certificate from the Municipal Civil Registrar of Mapandan. Home › Services › Death Certificate Description A death certificate is an official document that records the death of an individual. It is required for settlement of estates, insurance claims, pension benefits, and other legal matters. The Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) of Mapandan issues certified copies of locally registered death certificates. Requirements Medical certificate or certificate of cause of death Valid government-issued ID of the requesting party Barangay certification (for the requesting party’s relationship to the deceased) Procedure Visit the Municipal Civil Registrar’s Office and present valid identification. Fill out the request form and provide supporting documents. Pay the certification fee at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Receive the certified death certificate upon release. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) Classification: Simple Processing Time: 3–5 working days Fee: As scheduled by the MCR Where to Apply: Municipal Civil Registrar’s Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Birth Certificate • Marriage License • Name Correction (RA 9048)

title: Health Consultation — BetterMapandan.org
description: Free health consultation services for Mapandan residents at the Rural Health Unit. Walk-in services available for all residents.
body: Health, Social Welfare & Agriculture Health Consultation Free health consultation services for Mapandan residents at the Rural Health Unit. Walk-in services available for all residents. Home › Services › Health Consultation Description The Municipal Health Office (MHO) / Rural Health Unit (RHU) provides free health consultation services to all residents of Mapandan. This includes general medical consultations, health advice, and referrals to higher-level health facilities when necessary. Walk-in patients are served on a first-come, first-served basis. Requirements None — open to all residents Procedure Visit the Rural Health Unit (RHU) in Poblacion during office hours. Register at the reception counter and provide your basic information. Wait for your name to be called for consultation. Consult with the attending physician or health officer. Receive prescription or referrals, if applicable. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Health Office (MHO / RHU) Classification: Simple Processing Time: Walk-in (same day) Fee: Free Where to Apply: Rural Health Unit, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1874 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Sanitary Permit • AICS Assistance

title: Transfer of Land Ownership — BetterMapandan.org
description: Transfer land ownership in Mapandan. Learn about the requirements, procedures, and fees for property transfer at the Assessor's Office.
body: Real Property & Revenue Administration Transfer of Land Ownership Transfer land ownership in Mapandan. Learn about the requirements, procedures, and fees for property transfer at the Assessor's Office. Home › Services › Transfer of Land Ownership Description Transfer of land ownership is the legal process of transferring property rights from one owner to another. This process involves coordination between the Municipal Assessor’s Office (MASSO) and the Municipal Treasury Office (MTO) to update property records and ensure proper tax assessment. The transfer may be due to sale, donation, inheritance, or other legal means. Requirements Deed of sale or deed of donation (depending on transfer type) Tax clearance from the Municipal Treasurer’s Office Valid government-issued ID of the new owner Original tax declaration Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) certificate of registration Procedure Secure a tax clearance from the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Obtain the BIR certificate of registration for the transfer. Submit all required documents to the Municipal Assessor’s Office (MASSO). Pay the assessor’s fee based on the property value. Wait for processing and verification of documents. Receive the updated tax declaration under the new owner’s name. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Assessor’s Office (MASSO) + Municipal Treasury Office (MTO) Classification: Complex Processing Time: 15–30 working days Fee: Varies (assessor’s fee based on property value) Where to Apply: Municipal Assessor’s Office, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Real Property Tax Payment • Tax Declaration Copy

title: Marriage License — BetterMapandan.org
description: Requirements, fees, and step-by-step procedure for applying for a marriage license in the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan.
body: Civil Registry & Vital Records Marriage License Apply for a marriage license at the Municipal Civil Registrar of Mapandan, Pangasinan. Home › Services › Marriage License Description A marriage license is a legal requirement before a marriage can be solemnized in the Philippines. The Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) of Mapandan processes marriage license applications, which include a required publication period. The license is valid for 120 days from the date of issuance. Requirements Birth certificates (PSA-authenticated) of both contracting parties Valid government-issued IDs of both parties Certificate of No Marriage (CENOMAR) for both parties Parental consent or advice (if either party is under 25 years old) Certificate of Marriage Counseling (from a government-accredited counselor) Community Tax Certificate (cedula) for both parties Two (2) ID photos of each party Procedure Both parties appear at the MCR and submit all required documents. Fill out the marriage license application form. Pay the applicable fees at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Wait for the 10-day publication period. After publication, claim the marriage license from the MCR. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) Classification: Simple Processing Time: 10–15 working days (including 10-day publication period) Fee: As scheduled by the MCR Where to Apply: Municipal Civil Registrar’s Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Birth Certificate • Death Certificate • Name Correction (RA 9048)

title: Name Correction (RA 9048) — BetterMapandan.org
description: Requirements, fees, and step-by-step procedure for correcting a clerical or typographical error in a birth certificate under RA 9048 in Mapandan, Pangasinan.
body: Civil Registry & Vital Records Name Correction (RA 9048) Correct clerical or typographical errors in your birth certificate under Republic Act No. 9048. Home › Services › Name Correction (RA 9048) Description Republic Act No. 9048 authorizes the city or municipal civil registrar to correct clerical or typographical errors in civil registry entries without the need for a judicial order. This covers corrections in first names, nicknames, or minor spelling errors. This process does not apply to changes in gender, date of birth, or other substantive entries. Requirements PSA-authenticated birth certificate (original and photocopy) Valid government-issued ID of the petitioner Supporting documents that prove the correct name (e.g., school records, baptismal certificate, IDs) Notarized affidavit of the petitioner explaining the error Publication of the correction in a local newspaper (for the required period) Procedure Visit the Municipal Civil Registrar’s Office and submit all required documents. File the petition for correction of clerical error. Pay the required fees at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Wait for the publication period to be completed. After publication and verification, claim the corrected birth certificate from the MCR. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) Classification: Complex Processing Time: 15–30 working days (including publication period) Fee: As scheduled by the MCR (includes publication cost) Where to Apply: Municipal Civil Registrar’s Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Birth Certificate • Marriage License • Death Certificate

description: Requirements, fees, and step-by-step procedure for obtaining an occupancy permit in the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan.
body: Building, Engineering & Zoning Occupancy Permit Obtain an occupancy permit to legally occupy a newly constructed or renovated building in Mapandan. Home › Services › Occupancy Permit Description An occupancy permit certifies that a building or structure has been completed and inspected in accordance with the approved plans and the National Building Code. It is required before any building may be legally occupied or used. Requirements Approved building permit As-built plans (reflecting the actual construction) Inspection report from the Municipal Engineering Office Fire safety inspection certificate from the Bureau of Fire Protection Procedure Request a final inspection from the Municipal Engineering Office. Submit the as-built plans and inspection report. Obtain a fire safety inspection certificate from the BFP. Submit all documents to the MEO for review. Receive the occupancy permit upon approval. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Engineering Office (MEO) Classification: Simple Processing Time: 3–5 working days Fee: As scheduled by the MEO Where to Apply: Municipal Engineering Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Zoning Clearance • Building Permit

title: Real Property Tax Payment — BetterMapandan.org
description: Pay your real property tax obligations in Mapandan. Learn about assessment rates, fees, and step-by-step payment procedures.
body: Real Property & Revenue Administration Real Property Tax Payment Pay your real property tax obligations in Mapandan. Learn about assessment rates, fees, and step-by-step payment procedures. Home › Services › Real Property Tax Payment Description Real property tax (RPT) is an annual tax on the assessed value of land, buildings, and improvements owned by individuals or entities within the Municipality of Mapandan. Payment of RPT is required under the Local Government Code (Republic Act No. 7160) and Provincial Ordinance No. 253-2020. The tax is used to fund local services, infrastructure, and public welfare programs. Requirements Tax declaration from the Municipal Assessor’s Office Previous year’s official receipt Valid government-issued ID Procedure Present your tax declaration and previous year’s official receipt at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Verify the current assessed value of your property with the assessor. Pay the corresponding real property tax at the treasury counter. Receive your official receipt as proof of payment. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Treasury Office (MTO) Classification: Simple Processing Time: Same day Fee: Based on assessed value (1% annual for basic, additional for SEF) Where to Apply: 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter / Provincial Ordinance No. 253-2020 Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Cedula / Community Tax Certificate • Tax Declaration Copy • Transfer of Land Ownership

description: Obtain a sanitary permit for your business in Mapandan. Learn about requirements, inspection process, and fees at the Municipal Health Office.
body: Health, Social Welfare & Agriculture Sanitary Permit Obtain a sanitary permit for your business in Mapandan. Learn about requirements, inspection process, and fees at the Municipal Health Office. Home › Services › Sanitary Permit Description A sanitary permit is required for all businesses that handle food, beverages, or other consumable products to ensure compliance with health and sanitation standards. The permit is issued by the Municipal Health Office (MHO) after an inspection of the business premises to verify that health and safety regulations are met. Requirements Health certificate from the MHO Food handler’s certificate (if applicable for food businesses) Business permit from the Municipal Treasurer’s Office Inspection of premises by MHO health officer Procedure Secure a health certificate and food handler’s certificate (if applicable) from the MHO. Request an inspection of your business premises by a health officer. Pay the corresponding sanitary permit fee based on your business type. Receive your sanitary permit after successful inspection and payment. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Health Office (MHO) Classification: Simple Processing Time: 3–5 working days Fee: Based on business type Where to Apply: Municipal Health Office, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1874 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Health Consultation • New Business Permit

title: Senior Citizen / PWD ID — BetterMapandan.org
description: Apply for a Senior Citizen or Persons with Disabilities (PWD) ID in Mapandan. Learn about requirements, eligibility, and where to apply.
body: Health, Social Welfare & Agriculture Senior Citizen / PWD ID Apply for a Senior Citizen or Persons with Disabilities (PWD) ID in Mapandan. Learn about requirements, eligibility, and where to apply. Home › Services › Senior Citizen / PWD ID Description The Senior Citizen ID and Persons with Disabilities (PWD) ID are government-issued identification cards that provide holders with benefits and privileges under the law. Senior Citizens (60 years old and above) and PWDs are entitled to discounts, tax exemptions, and other benefits as mandated by RA 9994 (Senior Citizens Act) and RA 7277 (Magna Carta for Disabled Persons). The IDs are processed through the MSWDO and MCR in coordination with the national implementing agencies. Requirements Birth certificate or PSA-issued document as proof of age (for Senior Citizens) Barangay certification of residency Two (2) pieces of 2x2 ID photos Medical certificate (for PWD applicants, indicating the nature of disability) Procedure Secure a barangay certification of residency from your barangay office. For PWD applicants, obtain a medical certificate indicating the nature and severity of the disability. Submit all required documents to the MSWDO or MCR office. Wait for verification and processing of your application. Receive your Senior Citizen or PWD ID upon approval. Service Details Responsible Office: MSWDO + MCR Classification: Simple Processing Time: 3–5 working days Fee: Free Where to Apply: MSWDO Office, Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1751 / 0930-641-3934 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services AICS Assistance • Health Consultation

Home › Services › Special Event Permit Description A special event permit is required for individuals or organizations planning to hold public events within Mapandan. This includes festivals, concerts, trade fairs, sports tournaments, and other gatherings that may affect public roads, spaces, or safety. Requirements Event proposal with detailed description, expected attendance, and schedule Sketch or map of the event venue Safety and security plan Event insurance (if applicable, depending on event type and size) Barangay endorsement from the barangay where the event will be held Procedure Secure a barangay endorsement from the barangay where the event will take place. Prepare the event proposal, venue sketch, and safety plan. Submit all requirements to the Municipal Treasurer’s Office (MTO) and/or Mayor’s Office. Wait for review and approval; pay any required fees. Receive the approved special event permit. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Treasurer’s Office (MTO) + Mayor’s Office Classification: Simple Processing Time: 5–7 working days Fee: Varies by event type and scale Where to Apply: 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services New Business Permit • Business Permit Renewal

title: Accessibility Statement — BetterMapandan.org
description: Accessibility commitment and standards for the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal.
body: Support Accessibility Statement Our commitment to making government information accessible to all residents. Our commitment Better Mapandan is committed to ensuring digital accessibility for people with disabilities. We continually improve the user experience for everyone and apply the relevant accessibility standards. Conformance Status We aim to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at the AA level. These guidelines explain how to make web content more accessible for people with disabilities. Measures Taken We have implemented the following accessibility features across the site: Semantic HTML structure Skip-to-content navigation link Visible focus indicators Sufficient color contrast (4.5:1 minimum) Keyboard-accessible navigation Screen-reader-friendly labels Descriptive link text Proper heading hierarchy Accessibility features Keyboard Navigation All interactive elements are accessible via keyboard. Use Tab to move between elements, Enter to activate links and buttons, and Escape to close overlays. Screen Readers The site uses semantic HTML, ARIA labels, and proper heading hierarchy to ensure screen readers can navigate the content effectively. Color & Contrast All text meets WCAG AA contrast requirements. Information is never conveyed through color alone — icons, labels, and text are always provided alongside color coding. Text Resizing The site uses relative units (rem, em) for text sizing. Users can resize text up to 200% without loss of content or functionality. Forms All form inputs are associated with labels. Error messages are descriptive and programmatically associated with the relevant input fields. Tables Data tables include proper header associations ( <th scope> ), captions where appropriate, and are responsive on mobile devices. Known limitations We are aware of the following accessibility limitations and are working to address them: PDF documents: Some linked government documents (COA reports, provincial issuances) may not be fully accessible. We provide HTML summaries where possible. Interactive maps: The Leaflet map is navigable via keyboard but may present challenges for screen reader users. We provide alternative text descriptions and a data table fallback. Third-party content: Embedded content from external government websites may not meet the same accessibility standards. Feedback We welcome your feedback on the accessibility of Better Mapandan. If you encounter accessibility barriers, please let us know: Report an Issue Use our reporting form to describe the accessibility issue, the page URL, and your browser/device information. Report accessibility issue → GitHub Issues Developers can file accessibility issues directly on our GitHub repository. Open GitHub issue →

title: Frequently Asked Questions — BetterMapandan.org
description: Common questions about government services, documents, and civic information for Mapandan, Pangasinan.
body: Support Frequently Asked Questions Answers to common questions about government services and civic information in Mapandan. General About Better Mapandan Is this an official government website? No. Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal built and maintained by volunteers. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Municipality of Mapandan or any government agency. For official information, visit mapandan.gov.ph . How is this project funded? Better Mapandan is entirely volunteer-run and uses no government funding. The cost to the people of Mapandan is ₱0. Hosting and domain costs are covered by the BetterGov.ph initiative. Where does the data come from? All data is compiled from publicly available government sources: COA audit reports, PSA census data, DILG disclosures, BLGF treasury data, provincial issuances, and municipal announcements. Every source is attributed on the page where the data appears. How do I report incorrect information? Visit our Report Incorrect Information page. Provide the page URL, the specific error, and the correct information if known. Our volunteers will review and update the data. Services Government services How do I get a birth certificate? Visit the Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) at the 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion. Bring a valid ID and the required fee. Processing time is typically 3–5 working days. See the full requirements on the Birth Certificate service page . How do I apply for a business permit? Visit the Municipal Treasurer's Office (MTO) with your DTI/SEC registration, barangay clearance, and other required documents. New permits are processed in 3–5 working days. See the Business Permit service page for full details. How do I get a building permit? Apply through the Municipal Engineering Office (MEO). Building permits require a zoning clearance, architectural plans, and structural plans. Processing takes 10–15 working days. See the Building Permit service page . How do I request a barangay clearance? Visit your barangay hall with a valid ID. Barangay clearances are typically issued the same day. This is often a prerequisite for other government transactions. Data & Transparency Data questions What does "Placeholder" mean on data? Some data is marked as "Placeholder" when the exact figure is not yet available from official sources. We use reasonable estimates based on available data and clearly mark these so residents know the difference between verified and estimated figures. How often is the data updated? Each data section includes a "Last updated" timestamp. Major updates happen when new COA audit reports, PSA census data, or municipal financial disclosures become available. The site is continuously improved by volunteers. Can I download the data? Yes. The Statistics page includes CSV download options for chart data. The Transparency page provides links to source documents. All data is publicly available and free to reuse under open data principles. How can I verify the data myself? Every data section includes a source attribution and, where available, a link to the original document. You can cross-reference with official sources like the COA website, PSA, or the municipal government directly. Contact Still have questions? For government services Contact the relevant office directly. See the Government Directory for phone numbers and email addresses. For this website Report issues, suggest improvements, or contribute on GitHub . For data corrections, use the Report Incorrect Information form.

title: Privacy Policy — BetterMapandan.org
description: Privacy policy for the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal.
body: Legal Privacy Policy How we handle data on the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal. Overview Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal. We collect minimal data and are committed to protecting your privacy. Information We Collect Automatically collected: When you visit Better Mapandan, our hosting provider (GitHub Pages) may collect standard web server logs including your IP address, browser type, referring URL, and pages visited. This is standard server operation and is not used to identify individual visitors. Search queries: The search functionality runs entirely in your browser. Your search queries are never sent to a server or stored. Language preference: If you use the language switcher (when available), your preference is stored locally in your browser and is never transmitted to us. How We Use Information We do not use, sell, or share personal information. Server logs are used only for maintaining the website and understanding usage patterns in aggregate. Cookies Better Mapandan does not use cookies. The language preference is stored using localStorage , which is a browser-only storage mechanism and is not transmitted to any server. Third-Party Services The site loads the following external resources: Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com) — for font loading Open-Meteo API (open-meteo.com) — for weather data (loaded only on the homepage) Leaflet / OpenStreetMap — for the interactive map (loaded only on the homepage) These services have their own privacy policies. We do not share any personal data with them. Data Sources All government data presented on this site is compiled from publicly available official sources. This data is already public and is presented here for informational purposes. Changes to This Policy This privacy policy may be updated from time to time. Changes will be posted on this page with an updated date. Contact For privacy-related inquiries, please open an issue on our GitHub repository or use the report form .

title: Report Incorrect Information — BetterMapandan.org
description: Report errors, outdated data, or incorrect information on the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal.
body: Support Report Incorrect Information Help us keep the data accurate. Report errors, outdated information, or missing data. How to report Choose the method that works best for you. All reports are reviewed by our volunteer team. Option 1: Email Send an email with the following details: Page URL: The page where you found the error Error description: What is incorrect Correct information: If you know the correct data Source: Where you found the correct information (if available) Compose email → Option 2: GitHub Issue For developers and technical users, file an issue on our GitHub repository with the label "data-correction". Open GitHub issue → What happens next? Review: Our volunteers review the report within 7 days. Verification: We cross-reference the correction with official government sources. Update: If verified, the information is updated on the site. Acknowledgment: We credit contributors (unless they prefer anonymity). Verification status Every piece of data on Better Mapandan includes a verification status label: Official Data from official government sources (COA, PSA, DILG). Verified Data independently verified against multiple official sources. Community Verified Data confirmed by community members with local knowledge. Needs Verification Data that has not yet been independently verified. Placeholder Estimated data pending official figures. Clearly marked.
